newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends slightly down on Tokyo's fall.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends slightly down on Tokyo's fall.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed slightly lower in line with weaker Japanese prices, but trading remained lacklustre due to lack of participation from both producers and consumers, dealers said.
They said while weaker Japanese prices kept buyers at the sidelines, rains in crop areas in northern Malaysia which have affected tapping activity restrained producers from selling.
"We are having a situation where no one wants to take new positions," said a local rubber dealer.
Dealers said trading ranges will remain tight until fresh market-moving factors emerged.

At the close, December RSS1 buyer was quoted at 319 cents ($1.26) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, down 1.50 cents from Tuesday. December SMR 20 buyer was unchanged at 310.50 cents ($1.23) a kg.
Traders retained previous offer prices, quoting SMR CV at 366 cents, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 322, SMR 10 at 311, SMR 20 at 310 and drum latex at 237.
The INRO five-day moving average was 245.63 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Nov 12 against 245.49 on Nov 11. The daily indicator price was 245.55 versus 245.65.
